newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq ends higher as Fed leaves rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq ends higher as Fed leaves rates unchanged.

text.p: Nasdaq shares surged Tuesday, boosted by the Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term interest rates unchanged and by bullish expectations for industry bellwether Intel Corp, traders said.

The Nasdaq composite index added 22.64 points or 1.69 percent to close unofficially at 1363.88. The Nasdaq gains outpaced a 1.03 percent jump in the Dow industrials, which added about 75 points to close at 7303.

"The over-the-counter gave a strong showing of itself across the board. Secondary stocks were strong. On a broad scope, it was a strong day," said Jack Bayer, managing director and head over-the-counter trader at Oppenheimer & Co.
Semiconductor stocks rode a wave of optimism after Merrill Lynch said it expects Intel's revenue growth to rise to 36 percent annually from 30 percent annually, traders said.
Intel surged 6-1/4 to 161. Applied Materials Inc added 3-3/16 to 69-15/16 and Altera Corp jumped 3-1/8 to 51-1/2.

C-Cube Microsystems Inc's shares fell 5-5/8 to 19-7/8 after it warned that its second quarter earnings would be worse than expected. Overall, advancing issues beat declining issues 2236 to 1931 on total volume of 546 million.
